short.title: Alexandria's Lost Tomb Foundations Found #Shorts
short.hook: Foundations of a massive limestone structure in Alexandria's royal quarter - and it may be part of a lost Ptolemaic royal tomb.
script: Foundations of a massive limestone structure in Alexandria's royal quarter - and it may be part of a lost Ptolemaic royal tomb.
The site shows thick stone walls and a tunnel extending northward beneath the structure.
Greek archaeologists have been searching here for nearly 20 years, following ancient accounts of a royal burial complex.
The scientific committee suggests the building may have had a funerary purpose, linked to Ptolemy IV's royal burial plans.
Yet this remains a preliminary interpretation, not confirmed by definitive evidence.
Could this tunnel lead to a hidden royal burial chamber beneath the city?
Tap the link below for the full case file.
short.description:
A Greek archaeological mission uncovered limestone foundations in Alexandria's royal quarter, possibly linked to a lost Ptolemaic royal tomb. The site includes walls and a tunnel extending northward, with experts suggesting a funerary function. However, this remains a preliminary interpretation requiring further investigation. Much of the royal quarter has been lost to urban development and coastal change. Source: Gulf News, https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/ancient-discovery-in-egypt-raises-hopes-of-finding-lost-ptolemaic-royal-tomb-1.500759902
